mappings.note: 'visphaarit aham' is the writer's own coined image and the item asks its abhipray -- reading her bhasha-shaili. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: unlike the bare gloss of 'visphaarit' elsewhere in this chapter, here a whole authorial phrase has to be interpreted.
The stated cause of the father's anger towards the mother. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the text names the cause, no reaction to his authoritarianism is asked.
Why the father turned suspicious -- the text's own reason (ingratitude of his own people). Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: recall of a stated cause.
Odd-one-out among synonyms of 'yatana' -- a paryayvachi drill. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: it tests word-class knowledge, not the lesson's content.
What 'ghar' meant in her day (the whole mohalla) -- the passage says it outright. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a stated fact, not a stylistic appraisal.
Whom the college principal was exasperated with -- narrated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.

The state in which Mannu Bhandari was born -- author biography. The frame has no biography LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because a birthplace is not the prescribed text's vishayvastu.
Whose fiery talk stirred her (Sheela Agrawal) -- a named character fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the metaphor is in the stem but the answer is a person.
What she did during the freedom movement -- listed actions. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: factual life events.
Which storm was raging at home -- the father-daughter clash, as narrated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: it asks what happened, not how she judges it.
What the father wanted of her according to the passage. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: his stated wish, not a reaction to it.
Sheela Agrawal's contribution to her life -- enumerated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.

'ragon me khoon ki jagah lava bahna' is the lekhika's metaphor and the item asks its tatparya -- appreciation of her figurative language. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: it is not a narrated event nor a single-word gloss.
The father's greatest weakness as the text states it. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: recall of a stated trait.
Why the principal wrote to her father -- a narrated incident. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
Why the father flared up -- the principal's letter, as narrated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the cause is in the text, not a judgement on his temper.
The national mood in 1946-47 -- the policy puts the 1946-47 andolan at LO-1. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: historical setting stated in the text.
The marriage-eligibility bar in her family -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a custom the text reports.

WHICH qualities the father carried the ruins of -- the list is given verbatim in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: unlike the item asking what 'bhagnavasheshon ko dhona' means, here the metaphor is only the frame and the answer is a stated list.
Sheela Agrawal's teaching subject -- a fact about a character in the lesson. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: she is a figure inside the text, not the author's biography.
Which behaviour of hers made the principal summon her father -- narrated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
WHAT she called her mother (vyaktitvavihin) -- straight recall of the word used. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the companion item that asks WHY she used that word takes LO-2; this one only asks which word.

Authorship of 'Chitralekha' (Bhagwati Charan Verma) -- literary history about another writer. The frame has no literary-history LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because the attribution is not this lesson's content.

Gloss of 'nihayat', a word from the lesson -- a word's meaning in context, which the policy places at LO-1. Rejected C-H1.2: shabdarth is not one of the vyakaran categories (sandhi, samas, vilom, paryayvachi, muhavare, vakya-shuddhi and the rest).
Who praised her speech (Dr Ambalal) -- a named character fact. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.

Gloss of the single word 'visphaarit'. Rejected C-H1.2: a bare shabdarth is not a vyakaran category; and rejected C-H1.3-LO-2 because, unlike 'visphaarit aham', no authorial image has to be read here.
Gloss of 'varchasva' from the lesson's vocabulary. Rejected C-H1.2: shabdarth is not among the vyakaran item types this book routes to C-H1.2.

Naming the author of 'Ek Kahani Yah Bhi' -- author identification, i.e. literary knowledge about the writer. The frame has no biography LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because the author's name is not the text's vishayvastu.

Sheela Agrawal's part in forming her as a writer -- the text narrates it. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: it asks what she did, not how the writer's style conveys it. (Stem is corrupted: 'Sheela Jeevan' for 'Sheela Agrawal'.)

WHY she called her mother personality-less -- the writer's own verdict and her choice of that harsh word. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: the companion recall item already covers which word she used; here the reasoning behind it is the mantavya.
Why she and Sheela Agrawal were thrown out of college -- a narrated episode. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: an event, not an appraisal.
Why the father felt proud after meeting the principal -- the text gives the reason. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a narrated turn, not a reaction to his authority.
How Dr Ambalal helped her -- narrated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
Causes and consequence of her inferiority complex -- both are stated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: it asks for the text's own account, not an evaluation of how she presents it.
Describe the father-daughter relationship from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: an abhivyakti answer built from narrated content, with no call to judge the father or the writer's craft.

Three reasons she could not make her mother her ideal -- an evaluative response to the mother's silence, which the policy assigns to LO-2. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: the reasons are her judgements, not events.
Which side of her personality the piece shows (freedom fighter) -- follows from the narrated activism. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: inference from content, not appreciation of how she writes.

Naming the author of the lesson. The frame has no biography LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because the writer's name is not the prescribed text's content. (Duplicate in substance of the other author-naming MCQ in this chapter, different option set.)

Where her childhood was spent (Ajmer) -- the policy names Ajmer/Indore as LO-1 content. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: Ajmer is the setting of the lesson itself, not an external biographical datum.
The name of her Hindi lecturer (Sheela Agrawal) -- a character in the text. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: she belongs to the lesson, not to the author's bibliography.
The atmosphere at her home -- described in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
Why the father made her sit through the debates -- the stated reason. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: his motive is narrated, no judgement on it is sought.
What the drawing-room debates were about -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
The national mood after the 1942 movement -- historical setting given in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
Which complex became a knot in her mind (her dark complexion) -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: recall of a fact, not of her comment on it.
The complexion the father preferred in girls -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a fact, not a reaction to his prejudice.
The reason she gives for the father's suspicious nature (betrayal by his own) -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: it asks the cause the text supplies.
The mother was unlettered -- direct recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
